newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-TRINIDAD FLOP AGAIN IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TRINIDAD FLOP AGAIN IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIERS.

text.p: Jamaica and El Salvador made virtually certain of their places in the last round of the CONCACAF World Cup qualifiers on Sunday while Trinidad's more experienced team flopped again.

Trindad barely mustered a shot on goal as they lost 2-0 away to the United States in semi-final stage group one, a result which virtually ended their chances of making the decisive six-team round of the CONCACAF qualifiers.
They have one point from three games in a group that also contains Costa Rica and Guatemala.

Trinidad were outplayed despite the presence of several European-based players, including Dwight Yorke of England's Aston Villa, Russel Latapy of Portugal's Boa Vista and Jerren Nixon of Switzerland's FC Zurich.

Second-half goals by sweeper Thomas Dooley and forward Eric Wynalda gave the United States, playing before a crowd of just over 19,000, their second straight win in the group and their sixth consecutive clean-sheet in World Cup qualifying matches.
The top two teams in each of three semi-final stage groups qualify for the final round, from which three nations progress for the 1998 World Cup finals in France.
El Salvador need one point from two games in group two after beating Panama 3-2 at home with a goal two minutes from the end.
Gustavo Trigueros scored El Salvador's winner in the 88th minute, two minutes after Jorge Dely Valdez, brother of Paris St. Germain striker Julio who did not play, had put Panama back on level terms.
Dely Valdez had given Panama an early lead with Raul Diaz Arce and Wilfrido Iraheta turning the game around. All five goals came from headers.
Canada have already qualified from the group which also contains Cuba, the only team who can rob El Salvador of their place.

Jamaica hammered minnows St Vincent 5-0 at home in group three and also need a draw from their last game -- at home to Mexico -- to go into the last six. Even if they do not win, Honduras have to make up a difference of nine goals.
Theodore Whitmore scored twice in three minutes early in the game but Jamaica then had to wait until the 64th minute for their next goal when Paul Young scored with a shot on the turn.
Two minutes later, Peter Cargil pounced on a wayward pass to score the fourth with Stephen Malcolm finishing the scoring five minutes from time.
